description.narrative: The development objective of the Social Safety Nets (SSN) Project for Sierra Leone is to establish the key building blocks for a basic national safety net system and to provide income support to extremely poor households in Sierra Leone. The project has three components. The first component, development of systems for implementation of social safety net interventions objective is to put in place the building blocks of a basic national safety net system in Sierra Leone. It will finance the following activities: (i) design of a targeting system; (ii) development of a beneficiary registry; (iii) development of a management information system (MIS); (iv) set-up of a payment system; and (v) development of a grievance redresses mechanism (GRM) and anti-corruption measures. The second component, cash transfers to extremely poor household's objective is to provide income support to extremely poor households. The third component, project management and capacity building have the following two sub-components: (i) project management, to ensure efficient project implementation. It will finance routine project management for the delivery of cash transfers, and staff and operational costs related to development of SSN systems, and (ii) capacity building, to provide capacity building to key stakeholders involved in the implementation of the project. It will finance: knowledge exchange events; program and line ministry staff social protection (SP) training; line ministry equipment, goods, and services (including line ministry staff travel costs and technical assistance (TA) support); and studies linked to implementation of cash transfers as well as studies to enhance the social protection dialogue in Sierra Leone.
The project development objective is to establish the key building blocks for a basic national safety net system and to provide income support to extremely poor households in Sierra Leone.

title.narrative: Proportion of beneficiaries enrolled following the SSN three-stage targeting procedure

comment.narrative: <p>The original wording of this indicator was "Proportion of households identified through community targeting with PMT with data entered in the Beneficiary Registry. Wording revised at AF2. Original target surpassed 111 percent, and revised target surpassed 105 percent.</p>

title.narrative: Proportion of payments delivered on time

comment.narrative: <p>Baseline date is the original project approval date. Original target date is the original closing date. At AF1, because of the scale up and expected lower likelihood of achieving the target for this indicator, the original target was revised from 90 to 75 percent. At AF2, the original wording was also revised/simplified. The original wording of the indicator was "Proportionf beneficiary households in the four target districts receiving cash transfers by the 15th of every payment quarter?".?????? However, the definition of the indicator (timeliness) remained unchanged.</p>

title.narrative: Beneficiaries of social safety net programs

comment.narrative:
<p>Original wording - "Direct project beneficiaries (of which female)" was replaced at AF2 with the new standard core indicator and sub-indicators on female participation and unconditional cash transfers.</p>

<p>Original PAD gives female participation as a proportion, not as a nominal number.</p>

<p>Target increased at AF1, AF2, and AF3 manyfold, to reflect scale up.</p>

<p>Revised and final target surpassed at 106 percent.</p>

title.narrative: Proportion of beneficiary households below the extreme poverty line

comment.narrative: <p>Baseline date is the original project approval date. Original target date is the original closing date. End target revised from 70 percent to 65 percent at the time of AF3. However, the higher original target was surpassed by closing, at 125 percent. Wording was revised at the time of AF1 from the original "Proportion of beneficiary households in the four target districts below the extreme poverty line", to reflect the national coverage of the project brough in by the scale up.???????</p>

title.narrative: Proportion of cash transfer component related grievances resolved within three months of being recorded in the GRM database

comment.narrative:
<p>Baseline date is the original project approval date. Original target date is the original closing date. Target was reduced at AF1, but eventually the original target was surpassed at closing. Original target surpassed at 105 percent, and revised target surpassed at 136 percent.</p>
<p> </p>

title.narrative: Proportion of beneficiaries receiving communication materials on the SSN behavioral change messages

comment.narrative: <p>Introduced with AF2, revised with AF3. Target surpassed at 111 percent.</p>

title.narrative: Beneficiaries with access to cash transfers for COVID-19 response from the contigency finance

comment.narrative: <p>This indicator was introduced at AF3, for the emergency COVID-19 response.</p>

title.narrative: Proportion of valid complaints registered in the GRM by ACC Call Center

comment.narrative: <p>Indicator introduced at AF2. Target surpassed almost five-fold.</p>

title.narrative: Proportion of households with Persons with Disablity (PWD)

comment.narrative:
<p>Target surpassed at 177 percent.</p>
<p>Indicator was introduced at AF2 and provides the number of beneficiary households who include a disabled person. It was surpassed at 316 percent. The significant overachievement may be due to the fact that at the time of the baseline, the statistics on persons with disabilities was imprecise and was not able to capture the full number.</p>

title.narrative: Proportion of beneficiaries who receive cash transfer in the current payment period

comment.narrative:
<p>Indicator introduced with AF2, then reworded in AF3. Target surpassed at 103 percent.</p>
<p>Indicator registers coverage for each period (among the eligible), evidencing that benefits were received. This indicator adds information to the evidence for the achievement of the PDO, as it signifies the successful establishment of the cash delivery system.</p>

title.narrative: Implementation strategy of the Social Protection policy revised and launched (Yes/No)

comment.narrative: <p>Indicator introduced with AF2, and fully achieved. Strategy revised and launched in November 2022, when this indicator was de facto achieved.</p>

title.narrative: Social Protection Registry for Integrated National Targeting (SPRINT) operationalized

comment.narrative: <p>Indicator introduced with AF2. Activity completed and target met in 2022.</p>

title.narrative: Proportion of beneficiary data updates resolved within 90 days (Percentage)

comment.narrative: <p>Indicator introduced with AF2. Target surpassed at 133 percent.</p>

title.narrative: Proportion of beneficiaries' representatives issued with photo identification (IDs) (Percentage)

comment.narrative:
<p>Indicator introduced at AF2, and is measured in percentage.</p>
<p>Program IDs with photo were envisaged, but the activity was eventually only partially completed, because of breakdown of unique equipment and decision that it was not a cost-effective solution.</p>

title.narrative: Proportion of household representatives collecting the cash transfers who are women

comment.narrative: <p>This indicator was introduced with AF2 and in fact measure what the original PDI indicator on female participation intended to measure - that is, the number of actual heads of families or household representatives, collecting the cash transfers, who are women. The target was slightly reduced at AF3. The revised target was substantially achieved, at 89 percent. The original target wasot achieved, fell short at 75.8 percent.</p>
